title: Sonic handshake: predictive prefetch and compact tool-surface PRD sketch
content:
TL;DR:
Sonic handshake is a lightweight PRD sketch for an optimistic, predictive prefetch + compact handshake protocol between client SDKs, edge proxies, and the hosted inference runtime. Target: mobile and low-bandwidth clients that need sub-100ms perceived latency for short-turn interactive workflows and tool-calling. The core idea is to let the client advertise a tiny predictive "intent hint" (micro-profile), let an edge proxy or the runtime pre-resolve likely tool calls and partial KV prefixes, and return compact commit frames that allow the client to assemble progressive responses without blocking on full model decode.

Problem statement:
- Developers building mobile conversational features see two main pain points: (1) first-byte latency for short completion/interactive actions (e.g., completions < 150 tokens) is often dominated by network roundtrips and cold runtime setup; (2) tool-calling patterns (search, code-run, DB lookup) add additional sequential latency when callers wait for the model to finish before invoking tools, or when tool invocation blocks streaming.
- Existing hosted streaming designs either stream raw token deltas (low overhead but high tail latency) or batch aggressively on the server (good throughput but worse p95 for small requests).

Goals (measurable):
- Perceived first-response latency reduction: reduce median client time-to-first-meaningful-byte by 30% for mobile under 3G/4G simulated networks compared to current streaming baseline.
- Tool call latency: reduce median tool-call end-to-end latency (client->model->tool->client) by 25% for canonical search and DB call flows.
- SDK ergonomics: provide a surface where client SDKs can opt-into predictive hints with a single flag and minimal migration friction.
- Reliability: handshake must degrade gracefully to standard streaming if prefetch hints fail or are disallowed by customer policy.

Success metrics / guardrails:
- p50, p95, p99 time-to-first-meaningful-byte by client region and network profile.
- Rate of incorrect prefetches (prefetches that caused additional work but no benefit) capped at <=10% for A/B test cohort.
- Percentage of sessions using sonic-handshake mode (adoption) and rollback safety (ability to instantly disable).
- No increase in per-token unit cost by >7% unless matched by latency benefit.

User personas and use cases:
- Mobile inbox assistant: quick summarization and tool lookup for calendar times (short completions).
- Editor auto-complete: predictive code completions with occasional tool-run for lint/format.
- Customer-facing chatbots: low-latency tool orchestration (DB lookups) under constrained networks.

High-level approach / components:
1) Predictive micro-profile (client-side): a compact, opaque hint (<=128 bytes) the SDK can send with a request. Minimal fields: intent vector id (hashed), expected max tokens, tool-likelihood map (tool ids + small score), client latency preference (latency-first | cost-first). The SDK will expose a boolean flag preferSonicHandshake and an optional prefetchHints object.

2) Edge/Proxy layer: the edge receives the micro-profile and uses a lightweight policy to pre-resolve: warm KV cache, fetch frequently-used tool results (search top-N), and prime model KV cache for expected prefixes. The edge communicates with runtime via a compact prefetch RPC. Edge decisions are policy-driven and subject to data residency / privacy controls.

3) Compact commit frames (runtime -> client): instead of waiting for full decode, runtime emits small frames that carry either incremental tokens (as now) or compact delta frames with pre-resolved tool stubs and prefetch confirmations. Frames include a prefetch-id to allow client-side correlation and safe replay.

4) Tool-call choreography: allow the runtime to return an optimistic tool-result stub when prefetch confidence > threshold. The SDK can choose to accept optimistic stubs (optimistic=true) or require strict validation. When optimistic stubs are used, the SDK will receive a later reconcile frame indicating whether the stub was replaced or confirmed.

Protocol sketch (minimalist):
- Client POST /v1/generate with header X-RW-Handshakes: sonic-v1 and body includes prefetch_hints (base64 opaque).
- Edge prefetch rpc: /internal/prefetch?session=... returns prefetch_id, prefetch_status, primed_kv_keys, tool_stub_refs.
- Runtime streams: { frame_type: "delta" | "prefetch_ack" | "tool_stub" | "reconcile" , prefetch_id: "...", payload: ... }
- SDK semantics: frames can be applied incrementally. If a reconcile frame contradicts an optimistic stub, the SDK raises a small delta event and provides application hooks for reconciliation (default: append reconciliation note to transcript).

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing surface):
- SDK option: preferSonicHandshake: boolean (default false). Quick migration: keep existing code path unchanged until flag enabled.
- prefetchHints: optional map, structure: { "intent_hint": string, "expected_tokens": int, "tool_scores": [{"id": "search", "score": 0.6}, ...] } - SDKs will provide helper heuristics to auto-generate this from common primitives (last user message, turn type) to minimize developer burden.
- Reconciliation callback: onPrefetchConfirm(prefetch_id, details), onPrefetchReject(prefetch_id, reason), onToolReconcile(tool_id, status, final_payload).
- Telemetry hooks: each requested session includes X-RW-Prefetch-Score header set by SDK for calibration metrics.

Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics to emit: prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success_rate, prefetch_false_positive_rate, prefetch_cost_delta, tool_stub_confirm_rate, reconcile_latency.
- Trace correlation: prefetch_id must be plumbed to tracing spans (edge->runtime).
- Sampling: default 1% full-fidelity sampling, 25% host-side metrics for prefetch-heartbeats.

Safety, policy, and degradation:
- Customer controls: customer can opt-out of prefetch at account level, org level, or call-level. For private deployments (VPC/on-prem) prefetch is disabled by default.
- Data controls: prefetch must respect KMS/HSM rules and not send PII to third-party toollets. Edge prefetch decisions should be recorded and auditable.
- Degrade to baseline: if any step fails (edge unavailable, prefetch timeout), runtime falls back to standard streaming. No request should fail due to prefetch subsystem errors.

Rollout plan (staged):
- Alpha: internal-only SDK + synthetic lab tests (1-2 weeks). Focus: correctness of frames and reconcilers. Linked PR: runtime PR #512 (see artifacts).
- Beta: opt-in for selected customers with mobile-heavy workloads. A/B experiments to measure p50/p95 latency and false-positive prefetch rate.
- GA: enable flag in Console with safe kill-switch and quota accounting for prefetch resources.

Open questions / risks (brainstorm list):
- Prefetch correctness vs. wasted work: how to balance edge compute cost and user latency benefits? Need simulation run on historical traces (Jira INF-2234).
- Security: can prefetch hint leak sensitive context? Need static analysis and a whitelist enforced at edge.
- Observability volume: prefetching will increase internal QPS for some patterns. Estimate additional load from alpha lab runs.
- SDK ergonomics: how much to auto-generate prefetch hints vs. require explicit developer input? Risk: buyer confusion if magical heuristics change app behavior.

Implementation notes and quick wins:
- Start with a purely server-side synthesized prefetch policy using existing session context; require SDK opt-in later. This reduces SDK churn while letting runtime teams validate approach.
- Reuse existing streaming frame envelopes but add two new small frame types (prefetch_ack, tool_stub) to avoid protocol churn.
- Add a cheap prefetch scoring service in edge that uses historical hits to decide whether to prefetch top-1 tool result only (limit scope first).

Immediate next steps (this doc owner):
- [ ] Run lightweight simulator on 7 days of production traces to estimate prefetch hit rate and wasted work. (owner: Miguel O, due: 2025-01-12). Jira: INF-2234.
- [ ] Prototype compact frames in runtime branch (PR 512) and add unit tests for reconcile flows (owner: Liam C, due: 2024-12-20).
- [ ] Draft SDK API PRs for JS, iOS, Android with opt-in flags and default helpers (owner: Priya D, due: 2025-01-05).
- [ ] Security review with privacy team for hint surface area (owner: Asha N, due: 2025-01-10).

Notes to self / brainstorming crumbs:
- "sonic" naming because the client experiences perceived speed improvements even if absolute network RTT unchanged. Consider other names if marketing dislikes.
- Could expand to include speculative quantization profiles for mobile to further reduce size of frames.
- Consider metric "client-perceived-commit" which is a product metric: time until user can act on partial output.

References & artifacts:
- See runtime PR #512 for early frame plumbing (linked_artifacts).
- Slack thread: #eng-hosted-api "sonic-handshake" for discussion notes (linked_artifacts).

End of draft. Feedback welcome — especially from runtime and SDK leads on reconciliation UX and worst-case failure semantics.
